expectations.text: Uses useState for controlled open state with open={state}
expectations.evidence: Line 19: `const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);` and line 34: `<Dialog open={open} ...>`. The dialog is fully controlled via useState.

expectations.text: Dialog has a label prop for accessibility
expectations.evidence: Line 35: `label="Delete project"` is set on the Dialog component.

expectations.text: Uses onHide handler to set state to false
expectations.evidence: Line 36: `onHide={() => setOpen(false)}` on the Dialog component. The explanation also states: 'Clicking the built-in close button (X) in the header fires the onHide event, which sets open to false' and 'Pressing Escape also fires onHide.'
Line 44: `<Button variant="danger" onClick={handleDelete}>Delete</Button>`. The trigger button on line 29 also uses variant="danger".

expectations.text: Uses slot='footer' on the button container
expectations.evidence: Line 40: `<div slot="footer" className="wa-cluster wa-justify-content-end wa-gap-xs">` wraps both Cancel and Delete buttons.

expectations.text: Does NOT use hide() directly -- uses requestClose() or state setter
expectations.evidence: No calls to `.hide()` or `dialog.hide()` anywhere in the code. All close paths use `setOpen(false)`: the Cancel button (line 42), the onHide handler (line 36), and the handleDelete function (line 24).

claims.claim: Three close paths exist: Cancel button, X button via onHide, and Escape key via onHide
claims.evidence: Cancel button calls setOpen(false) directly (line 42), and onHide={() => setOpen(false)} (line 36) handles both the X button and Escape key.

claims.claim: wa-cluster and wa-justify-content-end utility classes right-align the buttons with consistent spacing
claims.evidence: These are WA utility classes that should work as described, but cannot be visually verified from code alone.

claims.claim: variant='danger' renders the button in red/danger color from Web Awesome theme tokens
claims.evidence: This is standard Web Awesome Button behavior. The variant='danger' prop maps to WA's danger color scheme.

suggestions.assertion: Uses slot='footer' on the button container
suggestions.reason: This checks that slot='footer' exists but not that it is on the correct element. A response could put slot='footer' on a random span and still pass. Consider checking that it wraps the action buttons specifically.

No assertion checks whether the response uses Kigumi wrappers (import from '@/components/ui') versus raw <wa-dialog> and <wa-button> tags. The response happens to use Kigumi wrappers correctly, but a response using raw WA tags would pass all 6 expectations. Given the project memory note 'Skills must use Kigumi wrappers', this is worth asserting.

No assertion checks that className is used instead of class on the div with slot='footer'. The response uses className (React convention) on a plain div, which is correct. However, the project rule 'class not className on wa-* elements' is nuanced. An assertion verifying that wa-* elements use class while plain HTML elements use className would catch a common mistake.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover the core dialog control pattern well. The biggest gap is not checking for Kigumi wrapper imports vs raw wa-* tags, which is a stated project requirement.
